classes.section: Customer rate classes: summary table and SGS/MGS/LGS rate schedules
classes.text: Customer Rate Classes The cost of using Liberty's distribution network to deliver natural gas is determined by your rate class. You are assigned one of the six regulated rate classes: Rate Class Explanation Templates Minimum Monthly Consumption Maximum Monthly Consumption Small General Service (SGS) Residential customers who typically use natural gas for heat and hot water Single dwelling homes, individual apartment units n / A n / A Mid-General Service (MGS) Customers who typically use natural gas for small process loads and/or heat and hot water Apartment buildings, restaurants, churches, small schools - <250 GJ Large General Service (LGS) Customers who typically use natural gas for large amounts of heat and hot water and/or large process users Big box stores, large schools 250 GJ - Contract General Service (CGS) Customers who mainly use natural gas for process loads Manufacturing & processing facilities 1,000 GJ <10,000 GJ Industrial Contract General Service (ICGS) Customers who use natural gas for industrial process loads Large central heating plants, large industrial companies 10,000 GJ - Off-Peak Service (OPS) This rate is applied to any customer only consuming natural gas during the months of April through November - n / A n / A Changing Rate Classes "Rate Schedules" of Liberty Utilities Handbook of Rates and Distribution Services . Customer accounts are reviewed annually to ensure that they are not affected. You can request a change to the class by submitting a letter to us, outlining the rationale for the request. The request will be reviewed by our Customer Care Manager and a written decision will be provided to you within 30 days of receiving the request. Any changes to your rate will be made in the following year and will be noted on your next bill. Current Natural Gas Distribution Rates & Charges The cost of using Liberty's distribution network to have natural gas delivered to you includes features such as: customer charge, demand charge, and various types of rate blocks. Your rates depend on which rate class you fit into. The following rate structure and associated rates and charges are effective as of January 1, 2025. Customers are placed into one of the six regulated rate classes based on their monthly consumption patterns over the last 12 months. The classification of a customer in the SGS rate class no longer depends on consumption. The definition of the SGS rate class, which was approved by the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board and is shown in the Liberty Handbook of Distribution Services, includes: dwellings: a private suite of rooms used for living purposes in which the occupants have access to all rooms; dwelling out buildings; and individually gas metered, self-contained dwelling units within an apartment building. Mid-General Service Applicability Mid-General Service (MGS) Rates are applied to any customer requiring the use of Liberty's Distribution System to have a supply of natural gas transported to a single location, served through one meter. Service is limited to customers with a consumption less than 250 GJs per month. Effective Date: To apply to all bills rendered for natural gas delivered on and after January 1, 2025. *The rates quoted above are subject to adjustments that reflect all taxes including HST. Large General Service Applicability The Large General Service (LGS) Rates are applied to customers requiring the use of Liberty's Distribution System to have a supply of natural gas delivered to a single location served through one meter. Service is limited to customers with a consumption of at least 250 GJs per billing month. LGS RATES & TARIFFS* Monthly Distribution Customer Charge ($ per Month) For customers with max consumption < 650 GJs per month For customers with max consumption > 650 GJs per month 295.00 395.00 Monthly Distribution Delivery Charge ($ per GJ): For the first 250 GJs delivered per billing month For volumes delivered in excess of 250 GJs per month - between September 1 and April 30 - between May 1 and August 31 7.8120 6.5650 2.4689 Click here for the Utility Gas Current and Historical Commodity Rates Minimum Charge: The minimum monthly charge is the Monthly Distribution Customer Charge. The minimum annual charge will be imposed if the customer does not consume the qualifying monthly consumption requirement. The customer will be charged the difference between the actual annual distribution charges (customer or demand and delivery) billed and the amount that would have been billed under the Mid-General Service class, plus 5%. Term of Service: One year with automatic annual renewal unless the customer notifies LUG not less than 30 days prior to the annual roll over date and not more than 180 days prior to such date that service is to be discontinued. Terms and Conditions of Service: The provisions of Liberty Handbook of Rates and Distribution Services and the applicable Distribution Service Agreement apply to service under this Rate Class. Effective Date: To apply to all bills rendered for natural gas delivered on and after January 1, 2025. *The rates quoted above shall be subject to adjustments that reflect all taxes including HST.

carbon.section: CRA fuel charge rates: zero from April 1, 2025 and New Brunswick historical period
carbon.text: Fuel charge rates – Beginning April 1, 2025 On March 15, 2025, the Government of Canada made regulations that cease the application of the federal fuel charge, by setting all fuel charge rates to zero . For more information, refer to Notice FCN16, Removal of the fuel charge . Historical fuel charge rates – April 2019 to March 2025 Table 1 – Historical fuel charge rates for Alberta, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, Ontario, Prince Edward Island, and Saskatchewan The rates applied in Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, and Saskatchewan from April 1, 2019 to March 31, 2025. New Brunswick ceased to be a listed province effective April 1, 2020, and the fuel charge was reintroduced on July 1, 2023 . As such, the rates applied in New Brunswick from April 1, 2019 to March 31, 2020, and from July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2025. The rates applied in Newfoundland and Labrador, Nova Scotia, and Prince Edward Island from July 1, 2023 to March 31, 2025 . ops_page.section: Off-Peak Service Applicability and OPS RATES & TARIFFS (rate-schedule section)
ops_page.text: Off-Peak Service Applicability The Off-Peak Service (OPS) Rates are applied to any customer requiring the use of Liberty's Distribution System to have a supply of natural gas delivered to a single location served through one meter for the months of April through November. OPS RATES & TARIFFS* Monthly Distribution Customer Charge ($ per Month): 50.00 Monthly Distribution Delivery Charge ($ per GJ): For all volumes delivered per month: 5.6244 Click here for the Utility Gas Current and Historical Commodity Rates Minimum Monthly Charge: The minimum monthly charge shall be the Monthly Distribution Customer Charge. Minimum Annual Charge: There is no minimum annual charge. Seasonal Overrun Charge: Any volume of natural gas consumed during the months of December through March inclusively will be subject to a Seasonal Overrun Charge of $10 per GJ in addition to the rates applicable to this service. Term of Service: One year with automatic annual renewal unless the Applicant notifies Liberty not less than 30 days prior to the annual roll over date and not more than 180 days prior to such date that service is to be discontinued. Terms and Conditions of Service: The provisions of Liberty Handbook of Rates and Distribution Services and the applicable Distribution Service Agreement apply to service under this Rate Schedule. Effective Date: To apply to all bills rendered for natural gas delivered on and after January 1, 2025. *The rates quoted above shall be subject to adjustments that reflect all taxes including HST.
